questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.stem: [NEET 2021 | Chemistry] The number of molecules in 2.24 L of any gas at STP is:
questions.solution:
**Identify.** [NEET 2021 | Chemistry] The number of molecules in 2.24 L of any gas at STP is:

**Concept.** At STP, 1 mol of any ideal gas occupies 22.4 L and contains Avogadro’s number $N_A = 6.022 \times 10^{23}$ molecules.

**Relation.** $n = V/22.4$; molecules $= n \times N_A$.

**Work.** $n = 2.24/22.4 = 0.1\ \mathrm{mol}$.
Molecules $= 0.1 \times 6.022 \times 10^{23} = 6.022 \times 10^{22}$ (matches the verified option **6.022 × 10²²**).

**Option scan.**
✗ (1) 6.022×10²³
✓ (2) 6.022×10²²
✗ (3) 6.022×10²¹
✗ (4) 6.022×10²⁴

**Hence proved.** The verified option wording is **(2) 6.022×10²²**.

**Eliminate.**
✗ (1) 6.022×10²³ — That is $N_A$ for 1 mol (22.4 L), not for 2.24 L (= 0.1 mol).
✗ (3) 6.022×10²¹ — Off by an order of magnitude (would need 0.01 mol / 0.224 L at STP).
✗ (4) 6.022×10²⁴ — Too large — would need ~10 mol at STP.

questions.stem: For a Carnot engine between 825 K and 300 K, maximum efficiency is
questions.solution:
**Identify.** For a Carnot engine between 825 K and 300 K, maximum efficiency is

**Concept.** Carnot efficiency depends only on reservoir temperatures: $\eta = 1 - T_c/T_h$ (kelvin).

**Relation.** $\eta = 1 - T_c/T_h = (T_h - T_c)/T_h$.

**Work.** $T_h=825\ \mathrm{K}$, $T_c=300\ \mathrm{K}$.
$\eta = 1 - 300/825 = 0.636$.

**Option scan.**
✓ (1) 0.636
✗ (2) 0.364
✗ (3) 1.750
✗ (4) 1

**Hence proved.** The verified option wording is **(1) 0.636**.

**Eliminate.**
✗ (2) 0.364 — That is $T_c/T_h$, not $1 - T_c/T_h$.
✗ (3) 1.750 — Used $(T_h-T_c)/T_c$ instead of $(T_h-T_c)/T_h$.
✗ (4) 1 — η = 1 only for T_c = 0 K — impossible here.
